extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, applicants, institutional administrators, and NIH grant stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: A news feed summarizing recent NIH policy updates, resources, and guidance relevant to NIH grant applicants and awardees (policy changes, application-format guidance, review-process changes, and resource announcements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate models / New Approach Methodologies (NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease; investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes choosing models that maximize human relevance and translational potential; highlights NIH interest in NAMs but cautions selection should be driven by the specific research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants preparing DMS Plans for applicable proposals should follow the new 2026 pilot format and its simplified required elements (the announcement signals a standardized expectation for plan content and formatting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in research and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH is encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility; the Gold Standard Science plan and a new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative support embedding replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research, including key reminders for applications and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consider replication and reproducibility in study design, propose efforts that increase reliability, and note that replication/reproducibility may be a highlighted topic in applications and NIH initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive But Not Discussed (CBND) scoring designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains a modification to review processes: applications in the middle third may be scored as competitive but not discussed; applicants receiving this designation should understand its relation to prior cutoffs and review triage practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — application format and potential splitting into linked awards
rubrics_metrics.description: A 6-minute NIH overview video explains the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure, key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants for PF5 should follow the specified application format, be aware of the award structure, and understand that applications may be administratively split into linked awards after peer review and prior to Just-in-Time, per NIH procedures.
